In the days that followed, investigators discovered that Thomas had two prior arrests for burglary and operating while intoxicated. Neighbors and acquaintances also reported disturbing behavior in the days leading up to the attack, including an incident where Thomas allegedly tried to run over a woman and her daughter as a joke. A total of eight people suffered gunshot wounds during the attack, including a six-year-old boy and a five-year-old girl. And while some have been discharged after medical care, others will require multiple surgeries and ongoing care. Although officers brought Thomas down within five minutes of the first, 911 call, one question continued to linger. Why? What drove him to commit such a horrific act of violence? Investigators explored several possible motives, ranging from a failed relationship involving a woman from the LDS Church to financial stress and substance abuse, but most notably, a deep hatred toward the religious establishment and its rules. Investigators ultimately concluded that the attack had been carried out by Thomas alone. In February 26, DNR officer Luke Roberto and Granbach police officer Jason Carpenter were honored as heroes after Genesee County ruled their use of force against Thomas as justified. The families of the victims later released statements honoring the lives and impact their loved ones had on the community. 78-year-old Craig Hayden, 77-year-old John Bond, 77-year-old William Pat Howard, and 54-year-old Thelma Armstrong tragically lost their lives that day. Their memories continue to live on in the hearts of their families and the community they left behind. If you would like to support the injured victims and the families of those who lost their lives in this attack, you can donate through the GoFundMe page linked in the description.

Unfortunately, incidents like this never truly come to an end.
Instead, they leave behind permanent reminders of the devastating loss in the entire community suffered
because of one person's decision to choose violence.
In the days that followed, investigators discovered that Thomas had two prior arrests for burglary
Neighbors and acquaintances also reported disturbing behavior in the days leading up to the attack,
including an incident where Thomas allegedly tried to run over a woman and her daughter as a joke.
A total of eight people suffered gunshot wounds during the attack,
including a six-year-old boy and a five-year-old girl.
And while some have been discharged after medical care, others will require multiple surgeries and ongoing care.
Although officers brought Thomas down within five minutes of the first,
911 call, one question continued to linger. Why? What drove him to commit such a horrific act of
violence? Investigators explored several possible motives, ranging from a failed relationship
involving a woman from the LDS Church to financial stress and substance abuse, but most notably,
a deep hatred toward the religious establishment and its rules. Investigators ultimately
concluded that the attack had been carried out by Thomas alone. In February 26, DNR officer Luke
Roberto and Granbach police officer Jason Carpenter were honored as heroes after Genesee
County ruled their use of force against Thomas as justified. The families of the victims later
released statements honoring the lives and impact their loved ones had on the community.
78-year-old Craig Hayden, 77-year-old John Bond, 77-year-old William Pat Howard, and 54-year-old
Thelma Armstrong tragically lost their lives that day. Their memories continue to live on
in the hearts of their families and the community they left behind.

event_summary.short: Mass shooting and arson at a church in Grand Blanc, Michigan, on September 28, 2025. The suspect, Thomas Sanford, opened fire with an AK-47, set the church on fire, and claimed to have planted bombs at other churches. He was shot and killed by officers within five minutes. Four victims died and eight were injured.
